question: Where does the controlling function fit in the management process?

options.B: It is the final phase after planning and directing
options.C: It only happens during annual staff reviews
options.D: It is done alongside financial budgeting

explanation: Controlling comes at the end of the administrative cycle to evaluate whether initial plans were successfully achieved. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h1)

question: Why is controlling essential for nurse managers in resource-constrained environments?

options.A: It prevents resource wastage and ensures goal alignment
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for nursing supervision
options.C: It replaces the budgeting responsibilities of the hospital board
options.D: It automatically increases the monthly salary of staff

explanation: Monitoring activities helps managers catch deviations early, preserving scarce resources while maintaining care standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h1)

question: What is the very first step when starting the management control process?
explanation: Managers must first set a clear benchmark or standard before they can measure or evaluate any work. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h2)

question: A nurse manager notices high rates of catheter infections and audits the ward records. What is the next logical step?

options.A: Compare the infection rate data against the hospital target standard
options.B: Immediately dismiss the most junior nurse on duty
options.C: Write a new strategic plan for the entire hospital
options.D: Ignore the data because infections are inevitable

explanation: After gathering measurement data, the manager must compare it against the established standard before deciding on corrective steps. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h2)

question: Which type of control happens live while patient care is actively being given?
explanation: Concurrent controls monitor actions as they happen, allowing managers to correct mistakes immediately at the bedside. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h3)

question: Checking that newly hired nurses have valid licenses before they start work is an example of what control?
explanation: Feedforward controls anticipate problems and put preventive rules in place before the actual work starts. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h3)

question: What kind of measure checks if clinical steps like hand hygiene are being done correctly?
explanation: Process indicators track how care is delivered, focusing on clinical actions, protocols, and steps taken by staff. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h4)

question: Why must performance standards for clinical nursing care be realistic and measurable?

options.A: To make sure nurses never have to work night shifts
options.B: To ensure the hospital makes a profit every month
options.C: To prevent subjective evaluations and staff frustration
options.D: To eliminate the need for any patient feedback

explanation: Clear and measurable standards remove guesswork and bias, ensuring fair and objective appraisals for nursing staff. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h4)

question: What happens when nursing staff change their behavior just because they know they are being watched?
explanation: The Hawthorne effect describes how people modify their behavior when they are aware someone is watching them. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h5)

question: Which tool works best for finding hidden clinical errors and workflow problems in a ward?
explanation: Incident reporting captures unexpected events and near-misses that might otherwise be missed by routine observation. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h5)

question: Why should nurse managers investigate root causes instead of immediately punishing staff for errors?

options.A: To increase the speed of patient discharge procedures
options.B: To ensure that no disciplinary action is ever taken
options.C: To completely remove the need for any clinical standards
options.D: To fix underlying systemic flaws and prevent future occurrences

explanation: Looking beyond the individual staff member helps uncover systemic issues like poor training or faulty equipment. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h6)

question: What kind of work environment encourages nurses to report errors honestly without fear of unfair blame?
explanation: A just culture balances individual accountability with the recognition that systemic factors often contribute to mistakes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of quality assurance programs in nursing management?

options.A: Evaluating care delivery against recognized clinical benchmarks
options.B: Reducing the number of nursing training institutions
options.C: Eliminating all administrative paperwork in the wards
options.D: Maximizing hospital revenue from private patient suites

explanation: Quality assurance programs systematically assess clinical practices to ensure they meet established safety and care standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h7)

question: A surgical ward uses a checklist before operations to stop wrong-site surgeries. What type of control is this?
explanation: Surgical checklists are preventive tools used before an intervention starts to ensure safety standards are met. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h7)

question: What is a major barrier to effective nursing control in resource-constrained health facilities?

options.A: Complete willingness of all staff to adopt new rules instantly
options.B: An excess of digital tracking systems in every hospital department
options.C: Heavy workloads and chronic staff shortages leaving little time for audits
options.D: Unlimited financial resources causing confusion among managers

explanation: When staff are overburdened with patient care due to shortages, management control activities like audits are often neglected. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h8)

question: How can a nurse manager best overcome staff resistance when introducing a new control checklist?

options.A: Discard the idea of monitoring and let every nurse work independently
options.B: Involve frontline nurses in designing the tool and communicate its benefits
options.C: Impose strict salary deductions for anyone who questions the new form
options.D: Keep the new checklist completely secret until it becomes mandatory

explanation: Involving the team builds ownership and reduces resistance compared to top-down mandates enforced through punishment. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h8)
